guideSummary.surfnerd: Ovahimba is a long left-hand pointbreak buried in the middle of Namibia's Skeleton Coast reserve, and it may be one of the best yet least accessible waves anywhere. The area looks empty but teems with wildlife, and oryx, springbok, jackals, hyenas and even the occasional elephant or lion have been seen wandering down to the beach.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Yoff Beach is a mellow, forgiving beachbreak just north of N'gor, breaking over sand and offering up both lefts and rights. Long lines of crumbling whitewash roll in over a slowly shelving bottom, which keeps the wave less challenging than a lot of what's around.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Yoff Beach in Almadis is an exposed beach break that has consistent surf. Winter and spring are the best times of year to visit. Offshore winds blow from the south southeast. Groundswells and windswells are equally likely and the best swell direction is from the northwest. The beach break provides left and right handers. Sometimes crowded.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Yoff Island is a left-hand reef break that peels over an uneven reef off the coast. It comes into its own in bigger north swells, when the long left down the island really switches on. There's also a wind-exposed right about a five-minute paddle to the west that can run long and turn out excellent when it lines up.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Yoff Island in Almadis is an exposed reef break that usually has waves. Winter and spring are the best times of year to visit. Offshore winds are from the south southeast. Take care to avoid the rocks.
